chapters.title: Ticket views and the ticket list
intro: This chapter is for agents and supervisors who work through tickets in the **Tickets** module.
It explains queues and saved views, the ticket list, and how to update many tickets at once. It also covers the recycle bin and the **New ticket** form.

sections.title: The ticket workspace
intro: Open **Tickets** in the navigation rail, or press [[G]] then [[T]]. The ticket workspace has three panes.
Queues and saved views are on the left. The ticket list is in the middle. When you open a ticket, the customer's details appear on the right.

blocks.caption: The ticket workspace with the **My open tickets** queue and two tickets open as tabs.
blocks.alt: Ticket workspace with numbered highlights on the queues, the New view button, the tab strip, the filter box, the refresh button, a sort button and the New ticket button

callouts: **Queues**: ready-made ticket lists with live counts. A red count warns you about overdue tickets.
**New view**: creates your own saved view. Your views appear under **Views**.
The tab strip. The first tab shows the list. Each ticket you open gets its own tab.
**Filter by #, subject, customer…**: narrows the list while you type.
**Refresh**: reloads the list and the queue counts.
Sort buttons in the column headers, such as **Priority**.
**New ticket**: logs a new ticket for a customer.

list: Up to 12 tickets stay open as tabs. Each tab keeps its place while you switch.
Select **×** on a tab to close it. Select the **×** at the right end of the strip to close all tabs.
Select the panel buttons at either end of the tab strip to hide or show the left and right panels.
Drag the border between two panes to make a pane wider or narrower.

blocks.tip: To switch lists from the keyboard, open the command palette and type `Switch view`. See [Run a command from the command palette](#gs-command-palette).

sections.title: Queues
intro: Queues are fixed lists that every agent has. The number next to each queue is the count of tickets in it.
You only see tickets inside your role's data scope. Two agents can see different counts for the same queue.

rows: Open tickets that nobody owns yet.
Every open ticket you are allowed to see.
Tickets past their due time. The count turns red when there are any.
Open tickets close to missing a service target. The count turns red when there are any.
Open tickets that someone escalated, or that the service clock escalated.
Tickets in a waiting status, such as **Waiting on Customer**.
The recycle bin. Only people who may delete tickets see it.

sections.title: Open a queue or a saved view
sections.intro: Choose which tickets the list shows.
steps: Open **Tickets** in the navigation rail.
In the left panel, select a queue under **Queues**.
To use a saved view instead, select it under **Views**.
sections.result: The list shows the tickets. The heading above the list shows the name and the number of tickets.

blocks.tip: The address of the page names the list. Bookmark it, or share it with a colleague, to open the same list later.

sections.title: How saved views work
intro: A saved view is a ticket list that you define with conditions. For example, all critical tickets assigned to you.
A view always shows every ticket that matches its conditions. It never shows tickets outside what you are allowed to see.

rows: Everyone in the help desk. Only supervisors and administrators can share a view.

list: Each view shows how many tickets match it.
A star next to a view means it opens by default.
A view can keep its own column layout and its own sort order.
The owner of a view, or a supervisor, can edit or delete it. Anyone can copy it.

sections.title: Create a saved view
sections.intro: Build a list you use often, so it is one selection away.
prerequisites: To create a **Shared** view, you need supervisor rights. Without them, the **Shared** option shows **Needs supervisor rights**.
steps: In **Name**, enter a short name, such as `Critical tickets for me`.
Under **Who can use it**, choose **Personal** or **Shared**.

steps.text: Under **Conditions**, select **Condition**. Then choose a field, an operator and a value.
steps.caption: A personal view with two conditions: the priority is **Critical** and the assignee is whoever views the list.
steps.alt: New view dialog with a name, the Personal option and two conditions

steps: Repeat the previous step for each extra condition. Select the bin button to remove a condition.
Choose **All (AND)** if every condition must match. Choose **Any (OR)** if one match is enough.
In **Sort by**, choose the order of the list. In **Position**, enter a number to place the view in the panel.
Tick **Open this view by default** if this view should open when you go to **Tickets**.
Select **Create view**.
sections.result: The view appears under **Views** and opens at once. The message **View created** appears.

blocks.tip: In the **Assignee** field, choose the first option, your name followed by **(whoever views it)**. A shared view with this option shows every person their own tickets.

blocks.note: Select **Group** to add a group of conditions with its own **All (AND)** or **Any (OR)** choice. **Position** puts lower numbers higher in the panel.

list: Ticket: subject, priority, severity, status, status category, channel, language, sentiment, reopen count and satisfaction score.
Routing: department, team, assignee and brand.
Classification: category, subcategory, issue type and tags.
Service: SLA state, escalated or not, and entitlement.
Dates: created, due and last activity.

blocks.p: **Save the current column layout with this view** keeps the columns you chose for the list you were looking at. The view then opens with the same columns.

sections.title: Edit, copy or delete a saved view
sections.intro: Change a view's conditions, make a copy to start a similar view, or remove a view you no longer use.
prerequisites: To edit or delete a view, you must own it or have supervisor rights.
steps: Under **Views**, point to the view.
Select the **⋯** button that appears at the right of the view.

substeps: **Edit…** opens the **Edit view** dialog. Change the fields, then select **Save view**.
**Duplicate…** opens a copy named after the view with **(copy)** at the end. Change it, then select **Create view**.
**Delete** asks you to confirm. Select **Delete view**.

sections.result: The panel shows the changed view, the copy, or no view.

blocks.warning: Deleting a shared view removes it for everyone. Deleting a view never deletes its tickets.

sections.title: Which list opens by default
intro: When you open **Tickets** without choosing a list, SupportDesk picks one. It uses the first rule that applies.
There is one personal default per person and one shared default for the whole workspace. Departments and teams cannot have their own default.

steps: If the page address names a list, that list opens. This happens when you open a bookmark or a shared link.
On your first visit in a browser tab, your personal default view opens. Without one, the shared default view opens.
Otherwise, the queue or view you used last in this browser opens.
If none of these apply, **My open tickets** opens.
Under **Views**, point to the view and select the **⋯** button.
Choose **Edit…**.
Tick **Open this view by default**.
Select **Save view**.

blocks.note: A new personal default replaces your previous one. A shared default applies to everyone without a personal default.

sections.title: The ticket list
intro: The list loads 50 tickets at a time. Scroll down, or select **Load more**, to see more.
When tickets change while you work, the list updates itself. If you have tickets selected, a **New activity** button appears instead. Select it to reload the list.

rows: The subject. This column is always shown.
The current status, in its colour.
A countdown to the resolution target, such as **Breached 14d ago**. Resolved tickets show **SLA met** when the target was met.
The agent who owns the ticket, or **Unassigned**.
The customer organisation, with the contact's name below it.
**Channel**, **Department**, **Team**, **Product**, **Category**, **Severity**, **Created**, **Tags** and **Replies**. **Replies** shows agent replies and customer replies, such as `3 / 2`.
Bold subject with a blue dot
The customer replied and nobody has read it yet.
Red bar at the left edge of the row
The ticket missed its service target.
Open the ticket in the current row.
Select or clear the current row.
Open the next or previous ticket in the list.

sections.title: Filter and sort the list
sections.intro: Find a ticket in a long list without building a view.
steps: Open the queue or view you want to search.

steps.text: In **Filter by #, subject, customer…**, enter part of a ticket number, subject, customer or contact name.
steps.caption: The **All open** queue filtered by the text `POS`.
steps.alt: Ticket list with POS in the filter box and five matching tickets

steps: To clear the filter, select **×** in the box or press [[Esc]].
To sort, select a column header with arrows, such as **#**, **Priority**, **Due**, **Updated** or **Created**.
Select the same header again to reverse the order.
sections.result: The list shows only matching tickets, in the order you chose. The count next to the heading shows how many match.

blocks.note: **Due** always sorts the soonest due first. **Priority** always sorts the highest priority first. A saved view opens with its own sort order.

sections.title: Choose the list columns
sections.intro: Show the columns you need and hide the rest.
steps: Scroll the list to the right end of the header row.

steps.text: Select **Choose columns** (the columns button in the last header cell).
steps.caption: The **Columns** list. Ticked columns are shown.
steps.alt: Columns popup with check boxes and up and down arrows for each column

steps: Tick a column to show it. Clear it to hide it.
Use the arrows, or drag a column by its handle, to change the order.
Press [[Esc]] to close the list.
sections.result: The list shows the columns in the order you chose.

blocks.note: SupportDesk remembers the columns for each queue and view in this browser. Select **Reset** to go back to the standard columns.

sections.title: Update many tickets at once
sections.intro: Assign, close or tag a group of tickets in one step, instead of opening each one.
prerequisites: You need the bulk update permission. Supervisors and administrators have it by default.
You can update up to 500 tickets at a time.

steps.text: Tick the check box at the start of each ticket row.
steps.caption: Three tickets selected. The bulk actions bar appears above the list.
steps.alt: Ticket list with three rows ticked and the bulk actions bar highlighted

steps: To select every loaded ticket, tick the check box in the header row.

steps.text: In the bulk actions bar, select **Assign**, **Status** or **Priority**. For other actions, open **More**.
steps.caption: The **More** menu of the bulk actions bar.
steps.alt: More menu with Change priority, Add tags, Remove tags, Transfer, Watch, Close, Mark as spam and Delete

steps.text: Fill in the dialog that opens.
steps.caption: The **Assign tickets** dialog for three tickets.
steps.alt: Assign tickets dialog with Team and Agent fields

steps: Select **Apply**, or the action's own button, such as **Close tickets**.
Read the result, such as **3 of 3 tickets updated**.
Select **Done**.
sections.result: The list reloads. Tickets that could not be updated stay selected. The result lists each of them with the reason.

blocks.tip: Select **Clear** in the bar to clear the selection.

blocks.note: Without the bulk update permission, the bar shows a message instead of the buttons.

sections.title: Bulk actions
sections.intro: These actions are in the bulk actions bar and its **More** menu.

rows: Leave **Agent** empty to unassign. The team stays.
Pick from tags that already exist.
Adds you as a watcher of every selected ticket.
Needs the resolve permission. Customers are not asked to confirm.
Needs the delete permission. The tickets leave every queue.
Type `DELETE` and the number of tickets, such as `DELETE 3`.
Needs the delete permission. The tickets move to the recycle bin.

blocks.caption: The **Delete tickets** dialog asks you to type **DELETE 3** before **Delete** works.
blocks.alt: Delete tickets dialog with a box to type the confirmation text

blocks.warning: Closing, marking as spam and deleting affect every selected ticket. Check the selection before you confirm.

sections.title: Restore a deleted ticket
sections.intro: Deleted tickets and spam tickets go to the recycle bin. Nothing is lost until someone restores them.
prerequisites: You need the delete permission. Supervisors and administrators have it by default.

steps.caption: The **Deleted tickets** list. Here the recycle bin is empty.
steps.alt: Deleted tickets page with a filter box and the message The recycle bin is empty

steps: To find a ticket, enter its number or part of its subject in **Filter by # or subject…**.
Select **Restore** next to the ticket.
Select **Restore** in the confirmation dialog.
sections.result: The ticket returns to its queues with its conversation and history. A message offers **Open** to open it.

list: The list shows the newest deletions first, with who deleted each ticket and when.
A **Spam** badge marks tickets marked as spam. Restoring them also stops treating them as spam.
A **Legal hold** badge means a legal hold covers the ticket. SupportDesk keeps it for the hold.
The recycle bin is never emptied automatically.

sections.title: Log a new ticket
sections.intro: Log a ticket when a customer calls, walks in or writes to you outside SupportDesk.
prerequisites: You need the create tickets permission. Agents, supervisors and administrators have it by default.
steps: In the top bar, select **New ticket**, or press [[C]].
In **Customer**, enter part of the customer's name, code or e-mail address. Then choose the customer.

steps.text: In **Contact**, choose the person who asked for help.
steps.caption: The **Requester** section with a customer, a contact and the **Phone** channel.
steps.alt: Requester section with Customer, Contact, a new contact check box and channel buttons

steps: Under **Channel**, choose how the customer contacted you, such as **Phone** or **Walk-in**.

steps.caption: The **Request** section with a subject and a description.
steps.alt: Request section with Subject, Description, Attach files, Priority, Severity, Category, Subcategory, Issue type and Tags

steps: Choose the **Priority**. Add the classification fields and **Tags** if you know them.
Under **Product**, choose the product, module, version and installation if the request is about one.

steps.text: Under **Routing**, choose a department, team or assignee. Leave them empty to let routing rules decide.
steps.caption: The **Routing** section with an assignee chosen.
steps.alt: Routing section with Department, Team and Assignee, and the Keep my choice check box ticked

steps: Fill in any **Additional fields**, then select **Create ticket**.
sections.result: A card shows **#number created** with the customer's support eligibility. Select **Open ticket** to work on it, or **Create another**.

blocks.tip: If the requester is not in SupportDesk yet, tick **The requester is a new contact**. Then enter the **Full name** and an **E-mail** or **Phone**.

blocks.note: Select **Attach files** under the description to add files. **Create ticket** waits until every file has uploaded.

sections.title: New ticket fields and checks
sections.intro: Only **Subject** is always required. Your administrator can make some **Additional fields** required.

rows: The customer organisation. Choose it first to see its contacts and installations.
The person who asked. Choosing a contact also fills in the customer.
Tick it to add a person who is not in SupportDesk. An existing contact with the same e-mail address or phone number is reused.
A short summary of the request. Required.
What the customer needs: steps, error messages and impact.
How urgent the request is, and how serious its impact is.
Keywords. Type a tag and press [[Enter]].
What the request is about. **Installation** needs a customer first.
Where the ticket goes. Leave them empty to let routing rules decide.
Appears when you choose an assignee. Tick it so that rules do not reassign the ticket.
Fields your administrator added for the department.

blocks.heading: Checks before the ticket is created

blocks.caption: **Create ticket** without a subject. The **Subject** field shows **Enter a subject.**
blocks.alt: Request section with the Subject field outlined in red and the message Enter a subject

blocks.p: When a field fails a check, nothing is created. A message next to **Create ticket** asks you to fix the highlighted fields. Fix the fields shown in red, then try again.

rows: Whether the customer may get support for this request, such as **Entitled** or **Not entitled**.
The contract that covers the ticket, or **No covering contract**.
The department, team and agent that received the ticket.

blocks.note: If the customer is not entitled, a warning appears. A supervisor can override the entitlement from the ticket's **More actions** menu.

troubleshooting.cause: You do not have the permission to delete tickets.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask a supervisor to restore the ticket, or ask your administrator for the permission.

troubleshooting.problem: The **Shared** option in **New view** shows **Needs supervisor rights**.
troubleshooting.cause: Only supervisors and administrators can share views.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a **Personal** view, or ask a supervisor to create the shared view.

troubleshooting.problem: **Create view** shows **Give the view a name.**
troubleshooting.fix: Enter a name, then select **Create view** again.

troubleshooting.problem: The bulk actions bar shows a permission message instead of buttons.
troubleshooting.cause: You do not have the bulk update permission.
troubleshooting.fix: Update the tickets one at a time, or ask a supervisor to do it.

troubleshooting.problem: A bulk update shows **Not updated** for some tickets.
troubleshooting.cause: Each listed ticket failed a rule, such as a status that is not allowed next.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the reason next to each ticket. Fix those tickets one at a time. They stay selected for you.

troubleshooting.problem: The list shows **No tickets match your filter**.
troubleshooting.cause: Nothing in this queue or view matches the text in the filter box.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the text, or clear the filter with [[Esc]]. Try another queue such as **All open**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Create ticket** does nothing, and some fields turn red.
troubleshooting.cause: A required field is empty or has the wrong format. For example, **Subject** shows **Enter a subject.**
troubleshooting.fix: Fix each field shown in red, then select **Create ticket** again.

troubleshooting.problem: A new contact shows **Give an e-mail address or a phone number.**
troubleshooting.cause: A new contact needs a way to reach them.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter an e-mail address, a phone number or both.

troubleshooting.problem: An attached file shows **Blocked by the virus scanner**.
troubleshooting.cause: The malware scan found a problem in the file.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the file. Ask the customer for a clean copy.

faq.q: Why do I see fewer tickets than my colleague in the same queue?
faq.a: Each role has a data scope, such as your own departments. Queues and views only show tickets inside your scope.

faq.q: Can a saved view show each agent their own tickets?
faq.a: Yes. In the **Assignee** condition, choose the option that ends with **(whoever views it)**. Share the view, and each person sees their own tickets.

faq.q: Does deleting a ticket remove it for good?
faq.a: No. Deleted and spam tickets go to the recycle bin. Anyone with the delete permission can restore them.

faq.q: Why did the list not refresh when a ticket changed?
faq.a: The list refreshes itself only while nothing is selected. Otherwise it shows **New activity**. Select it to reload.

glossary.definition: A ticket list defined by conditions, such as all critical tickets assigned to you. It can be personal or shared.
The saved view that opens when you go to Tickets without choosing a list. It has a star in the Views panel.
A change applied to many selected tickets at once, such as assigning or closing them.
The Deleted tickets list. It holds deleted and spam tickets until someone restores them.
The part of the help desk a role may see, such as its own departments. Lists never show tickets outside it.
